To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the scene text detector can be effectively learned from weakly annotated or unannotated data.

1) we can train robust and accurate scene character detection models by leveraging unannotated or only weakly annotated scene text data, and 2) a regression-based deep network is more effective than a classification-based one for scene character detection.

we propose a weak supervision scene text detection method, which is able to train robust and accurate scene texts models by learning from a large amount of unannotated or only word/text line level annotated data, and achieve the state-of-art performance by using a small fully annotated training dataset.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the practical problem of training deep learning systems under weak supervision and provides a promising solution. the WeText can be applied to a wide range of scenarios, and it is an effective solution to alleviate the data annotation bottleneck.

the proposed method is able to achieve the best trade-off between the annotation cost and the detection performance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the weak supervision from unannotated/weakly annotated data can be a powerful tool for training robust scene text detection models.
the weakly supervised training can significantly improve scene text detection performance with a small amount of annotated training data, which may also benefit other vision tasks.
the weakly supervised scene character detector can serve as a powerful and effective tool for scene text detection, which is expected to greatly reduce the annotation cost for scene text data.
